title: Introduce safety-window provisioner and per-tenant QoS accountant
author: Sana Iqbal
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see short, unpredicted microbursts that cause transient SLA slippage for customers with tight throughput guarantees. Existing warm pools and burst tokens absorb many cases, but we lack a coordinated short-horizon reservation that (1) is cheap to maintain, (2) can be sized per-tenant according to contract, and (3) emits clear accounting signals for downstream billing and autoscaler decisions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: SafetyWindowProvisioner (a low-cost short-horizon capacity reservation layer) and TenantQoSAccountant (per-tenant obligation/debt accounting and telemetry).

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a SafetyWindowProvisioner controller that holds small, time-bounded slot reservations per pool to cover microbursts; a TenantQoSAccountant that tracks committed throughput vs observed throughput and exposes an SLO-debt metric and replenishment recommendation; wire-ups into the autoscaler to prefer using safety windows before triggering expensive provisioning; and a small observability surface (metrics, dashboards, docs, unit and integration tests).

Design notes: SafetyWindowProvisioner maintains sliding-window reservations of slots expressed as "safety-units" (abstract token representing N requests or X tokens). Each safety-unit has a TTL (configurable, defaults to 45s) and a lease weight mapped from tenant contractual priority. The provisioner opportunistically fills windows from underutilized pools and drains them when headroom is needed for long-running scale-ups. TenantQoSAccountant consumes per-tenant sampling from request routers and the pool occupancy exporter to compute three time-series: committed_rate, observed_rate, and slo_debt (committed - observed over a rolling 5m window). QoS accountant publishes a recommended safety-window size and an urgency flag used by the autoscaler to accelerate a minimal reactive scale (fast-path) or fallback to full provisioning (slow-path).

Compatibility and fallbacks: Default behavior is disabled for existing clusters; enabled via configmap flag dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true. When enabled, provisioner is conservative: safety units cannot exceed 5% of a pool's allocatable capacity unless tenant has a high-priority contract. On failure modes (controller crash, API unreachability) the provisioner gracefully releases reservations; autoscaler and request path have a deterministic fallback path unchanged from prior behavior.

Checklist (follow-ups and CI): - unit tests for provisioner lease lifecycle added - integration test in perf-canary harness added (simulates 3s microbursts) - dashboards: added example Grafana panels and alert rule for slo_debt > 5% sustained - docs: operator guide + flags - Linear: ENG-4321 (design/impl), ENG-5600 (telemetry/dashboards)

Commits (high-level): ["a1f4d3c: safety-window controller skeleton and CRD", "b2d7f91: provisioner reconcile loop and lease allocator", "c3e9ab2: tenant QoS accountant metrics and sampler", "d4a1b7f: autoscaler integration hooks (fast-path) and config knobs", "e5b2c33: tests: unit + perf-canary integration scenario", "f6c3d44: docs and grafana snippets"].

Key changed files (high-level list): ["services/provisioner/safetywindow/controller.go", "services/provisioner/safetywindow/api/v1alpha1/safetywindow_types.go", "pkg/qos/accountant/accountant.go", "pkg/autoscaler/fastpath/fastpath.go", "deploy/manifests/dedicated/safetywindow-config.yaml", "test/integration/perf-canary/safetywindow_microburst_test.go", "docs/operators/safetywindow.md", "docs/observability/slo-debt-dashboards.json"].

Review conversation (condensed): - Marco: "Nice separation. Two asks: clarify how we unit-size safety-units vs real request token counts, and make TTL config per-pool." -> Response: clarified sizing math in code comments and added per-pool TTL config (pool annotation) in commit b2d7f91. - Evelyn: "Concerned about double-counting capacity when safety windows overlap with warm pools." -> Response: added allocation reconciler so safety units account for warm-pool reservations; added tests to assert no overcommit in commit d4a1b7f. - Tomas: "Prefer exposed metrics to include label 'commit_source' (api|manual|linear-recommendation)." -> Response: added label on metric series in c3e9ab2. - Code owners: minor nits on naming and comments addressed in follow-up commits.

CI and stability notes: First CI run flagged a flaky integ test in perf-canary that simulates 10x burst patterns; reran with increased timeouts and it passed. Lint and unit tests green. E2E smoke in a dedicated QA cluster passed (observed reduced 95p latency for microbursts when safety-window was active).

Telemetry and dashboards: New metrics published under redwood.qos.slo_debt (gauge) and redwood.safetywindow.allocations (counter/gauge with labels pool/tenant/commit_source). Added a Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for per-tenant slo_debt, safetywindow fill ratio, and fastpath activation rate. An example alert: slo_debt > 0.05 for 10m triggers a warn and recommends linear-issue ENG-5600 follow-up.

Operational playbook (short): - To enable: set dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true, tune per-tenant contract multiplier in tenant-profile config, observe dashboards. - To troubleshoot: use /debug/safetywindow/leases and accountant diagnostic endpoint which returns recent commit/observed windows. - Rollback: flip the flag and the provisioner will release leases within TTL + reconciliation window.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals. No migration scripts required; CRD installed as part of manifests (safe to apply).

release_notes: Added SafetyWindowProvisioner (opt-in) to reduce latency during short microbursts and TenantQoSAccountant for per-tenant SLO debt reporting. Defaults off; operator flag dedicated.safetyWindow.enabled=true to opt-in. See docs/operators/safetywindow.md for tuning guidance.
notes: This PR is focused on short-horizon capacity smoothing; follow-ups planned to integrate billing signals and longer horizon predictive resizing (ENG-5600).
